fullmoon.html: At a Full Moon we see the whole face lit up because Earth is in the middle between the Sun and the Moon, and the Moon reflects sunlight.
A Full Moon is when the Moon is big and yellow.
newmoon.html: At a New Moon the Moon is between the Earth and the Sun, the lit side faces away from Earth, so we cannot see it.
A New Moon is when a new moon is made.
crescent.html: A crescent is a thin sliver of lit Moon seen near the Sun just after sunset. It comes just after the New Moon.
A crescent is when the Moon is full and round.
quarter.html: At a Quarter Moon half of its face is lit. It is called a quarter because the Moon is a quarter of the way around its orbit. There are two each month, the first quarter and the last quarter.
A Quarter Moon costs twenty-five cents.
gibbous.html: A gibbous Moon has more than half lit but is not full. It comes between a quarter and the Full Moon, and happens twice a month, waxing and waning.
A gibbous Moon is a kind of monkey.
waxing.html: Waxing means the lit part is getting bigger, from the New Moon to the Full Moon. It takes about two weeks.
Waxing is when you put wax on a car.
waning.html: Waning means the lit part is getting smaller, from the Full Moon to the New Moon. It takes about two weeks.
Waning is when the Moon gets tired.
moonorbit.html: The Moon orbits around the Earth. One trip takes about a month, 27 days, and the same side always faces Earth.
The Moon is far away and shines at night.
moonrise.html: The Moon rises in the east because the Earth spins, and it comes up above the horizon.
The Moon rises when it is dark.
moonset.html: The Moon sets in the west because the Earth spins, and it goes below the horizon.
The Moon sets when the Sun comes up.
lunareclipse.html: In a lunar eclipse the Earth is between the Sun and the Moon, so Earth's shadow falls on the Moon. It happens at a Full Moon.
A lunar eclipse is when the Moon blocks the Sun.
solareclipse.html: In a solar eclipse the Moon is between the Sun and the Earth, so the Moon's shadow falls on the Earth. It happens at a New Moon.
A solar eclipse is when the Earth blocks the Sun.
tides.html: The Moon's gravity pulls the ocean so the water bulges up, which is a high tide. There are two high tides a day.
Tides are caused by wind blowing the waves.
earthmoonsystem.html: The Moon orbits the Earth. It is about a quarter the size of Earth and is about 384,000 km away.
The Earth and the Moon are the same.
mooncrater.html: A crater is a bowl-shaped hole made when an asteroid hits the Moon. Many craters are billions of years old.
A crater is a hill on the Moon.
